segments.title: Tinsmith work on the cathedral and Jesuit church
segments.summary: Interviewers show photos of New Orleans churches; Picou says he worked in and out on the cathedral spires and slating, and on the Jesuit church domes, as a tinsmith.

segments.title: The bar building, its bandstand and the piano
segments.summary: Talk about how the back of the daughter's bar was once outdoors, the owner, big Joe moving the piano, the bandstand and its cabinets.

segments.title: Opening the scrapbook: Dixieland photo with Celestin and Alexis
segments.summary: They begin looking through the scrapbook; first page has a photo of Dixieland musicians including Chink Martin, Octave Crosby, Ricard Alexis and Oscar Celestin, plus a letter from a friend.

segments.title: Sancton article: High Society, Stearns, Bolden and the Paddock opening
segments.summary: Reading a clipping about Picou and Glenny, the Imperial band with Manuel Perez, how Picou worked out the High Society solo, the Paddock opening in 1949 and Marshall Stearns's visit.

segments.title: Los Angeles clipping: Picou sits in with Dizzy Gillespie
segments.summary: An article on Picou's visit to Los Angeles, his view of bebop and Dizzy Gillespie, his compositions and his dance tunes.

segments.title: The Onward Brass Band cap
segments.summary: A photo shows Picou in a brass band cap, which he says came from the Onward band.

segments.title: End of scrapbook, age, last job and unpaid TV fee
segments.summary: Picou is 82; his last public playing was a WDSU television show about two years ago, for which he says he was still owed $55.

segments.title: Albert-system versus Boehm clarinet
segments.summary: He has played both and prefers the Albert system for tone and ease.

segments.title: Bolden band members: Glenny, T-Bar, Bill Harrison
segments.summary: Picou recalls Albert Glenny as bassist and house painter, and other band members such as Bill Harrison on trombone, and later Happy Goldston at the Paddock.

segments.title: Playing High Society without keys; reeds
segments.summary: He explains he mostly plays on the holes, plays High Society with no keys, and scrapes his reeds with a knife.

segments.title: Leading his own early band
segments.summary: Asked whether he led his own band, Picou says yes; it was covered on an earlier tape.

segments.title: Mouthpiece, the French clarinet and its barrel
segments.summary: He has used only one mouthpiece his whole life, and describes the clarinet given him by a music store, from France, that was offered $1,500.

segments.title: The E-flat clarinet and parade playing
segments.summary: He explains the E-flat clarinet, its straight bell and smaller mouthpiece; an interviewer recalls hearing him in a parade with Old Man Barbarin on alto horn.

segments.title: Playing guitar
segments.summary: Picou says he was once a guitar king, still has his guitar, and disparages rock and roll guitarists.

segments.title: His younger brother Euless, singer and composer
segments.summary: Picou describes his younger brother as a good singer and composer of French and Creole songs who played guitar; he taught him.

segments.title: Playing at plantations and on trips
segments.summary: Asked about playing on plantations in the 1890s, Picou says he played everywhere with many bands but recalls no details.

segments.title: Closing remarks and recording details
segments.summary: Interviewer states the tape was made at the daughter's bar on November 3, 1960 by Bill Russell and Ralph Collins; the rest has no speech.
